title: WebSocket, SSE & XHR
lede: The realtime and legacy corners of the Networking surface — WebSocket, EventSource (SSE), and XMLHttpRequest. WebSocket and EventSource are Node's own (undici's), written in TypeScript; XMLHttpRequest is modeled as the spec's legacy synchronous mode. The fetch/Response/Request/Headers rows of this same status page are documented separately under the fetch surface.

entries.name: new WebSocket(url)
entries.signature: new WebSocket(url: string | URL, protocols?: string | string[]): WebSocket
entries.description: Both a client and a server-side WebSocket. The client is the global WebSocket as Node's (undici's): the constructor returns CONNECTING and the handshake runs on the event loop; messages arrive as MessageEvents whose binary data is a Blob or an ArrayBuffer per binaryType, and close()/onclose carry a CloseEvent (code, reason, wasClean). Server-side, attach klain:ws's `new WebSocketServer({ server })` to an http.createServer (ws://) or https.createServer (wss://) server and `wss.on('connection', socket => …)` hands each upgraded connection a WSConnection that coexists with ordinary HTTP. The raw Node `server.on('upgrade', (req, socket, head) => …)` event is also available for hand-rolled or non-WebSocket upgrades.

params.name: url
params.desc: The ws:// or wss:// endpoint (http:/https: are rewritten, as Node does).

params.name: protocols
params.desc: Subprotocols to offer; the server's choice is ws.protocol.

returns.desc: The client socket, an EventTarget with onopen/onmessage/onclose/onerror handlers.

differences: The client offers no `permessage-deflate` extension (Node's does), so `ws.extensions` is always `''`.

klain:ws's server-side `.close()` ends the connection without waiting for the peer's close frame. Its message events carry `ev.isBinary` and a byte-exact `ev.dataBytes()` (klain:ws's own API, not the client's).

entries.name: new EventSource(url)
entries.signature: new EventSource(url: string | URL, init?: EventSourceInit): EventSource
entries.description: Server-sent events (SSE) as Node's (undici's) EventSource, over fetch — behind `--experimental-eventsource` in Node. Covers readyState/close(), onmessage/onopen/onerror, and addEventListener/removeEventListener for named (event: name) records — data/event/id/retry field parsing, multi-line data: concatenation, the CRLF/LF/CR line endings, and auto-reconnect honoring a server-sent retry: delay while replaying Last-Event-ID. A response that arrives with the wrong shape (non-200, or without text/event-stream) fails permanently instead of retrying.

params.name: url
params.desc: The SSE endpoint to connect to.

returns.desc: The event source, with readyState, onmessage/onopen/onerror and addEventListener.

entries.name: new XMLHttpRequest()
entries.description: A legacy client modeled as the spec's synchronous mode: .send() runs the request to completion before returning, then fires every registered callback once. It's not actually blocking — .send() is built on the same non-blocking primitive fetch() uses, so it still yields the current fiber when called from inside an http.listen connection handler or a klain:sync worker goroutine (making pooled goroutines a real closed-loop load generator). Supports .open(method, url, async?, user?, password?) with async: false exact, .setRequestHeader(), .send()/.send(body), .abort(), .readyState, .status, .responseText/.response, .getResponseHeader()/.getAllResponseHeaders(), and the zero-argument callbacks. A network-level failure fires .onerror rather than throwing.

returns.desc: The request object, with onreadystatechange/onload/onerror callbacks.

differences: Modeled as the real spec's legacy *synchronous* mode: `.send()`/`.send(body)` runs the request to completion before returning, then fires every registered callback once, synchronously — there's no default-async, callback-interleaved mode (this compiler has no re-entrant-into-already-returned-caller callback machinery to support one).

`.open(method, url, async?, user?, password?)` accepts the optional `async` flag: `async === false` is exact (the request is already synchronous); `async === true` also blocks (no main-thread event loop to defer `.onload` onto) — a documented narrowing. The `user`/`password` args are accepted but not yet wired to HTTP auth.
`.setRequestHeader(name, value)` accumulates headers, but names are **not** lowercased here (unlike `Headers`' own methods) — a separate V1 narrowing.
`.readyState` is 0/1/4 only (UNSENT/OPENED/DONE); the real spec's HEADERS_RECEIVED/LOADING have no meaning for a transfer that always runs to completion in one call.
`.responseText`/`.response` are identical values — only a text `responseType` is supported; no `responseType` other than the default.
`.onreadystatechange`/`.onload`/`.onerror` callbacks are zero-argument (deliberately — a payload-carrying callback isn't representable for this particular type).
`.abort()` is a best-effort `readyState` reset — there's nothing to actually interrupt once a synchronous `.send()` has returned.
`.getAllResponseHeaders()` returns headers in arrival order, not the spec's lowercase-sorted order.
